provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Every input has exactly one marker cell. The marker is originally colour 8 (cyan), which becomes palette[8] in the visible grid. It sits at the centre of the 3x3 bounding box of one sprite. The output is that 3x3 window with the marker repainted in the sprite's colour. Under any D4 transform, the centred 3x3 window maps to the transformed window, and its centre stays the centre. So cropping directly around the visible marker yields the correctly oriented output with no orientation-specific logic. The colour roles are specialised as constants: background = palette[0] and marker = palette[8]. The sprite colour is the most common colour in the window, excluding the background and the marker. The generator keeps sprites at least one cell apart, so the window only ever contains the target sprite. If two colours tie for most common, the smaller colour value is chosen.
draft_notes.limitations: This assumes the background is palette[0] and the marker is palette[8], as in the constructor. The generator places the marker at the interior centre of a 3x3 box, so the window is always a full 3x3; at grid edges the code clips the window, matching the archived solver. If the window held no sprite colour besides the marker, which the generator should not produce, the marker is filled with the background colour. No fixture contradictions were found. These notes come from reading the code; I have not run any tests.
